chunks: Some of our companions, from the one who mentioned him, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿUmar ibn Abān al-Kalbī, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:
I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was born, the white lands of Persia and the palaces of al-Shām were opened up to Āminah.
Then Fāṭimah bint Asad, the mother of Amīr al-Muʾminīn, came to Abū Ṭālib smiling and rejoicing, and informed him of what Āminah had said.
So Abū Ṭālib said to her: Are you astonished at this? You will conceive and give birth to his successor and his minister.

key_terms.آمِنَةَ: The mother of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, to whom the vision was shown.
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, whose birth is being described.
key_terms.فَارِسَ: Persia, mentioned as part of the vision shown at the Prophet’s birth.
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ أَسَدٍ: The mother of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, who brought the news to Abū Ṭālib.
key_terms.قُصُورُ الشَّامِ: The palaces of al-Shām, mentioned among the signs revealed.
key_terms.وَزِيرِهِ: His minister or helper, referring to the close supporting role of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام.
key_terms.وَصِيِّهِ: His successor, referring to the designated successor of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kāfī narrate about the signs at the Prophet’s birth and the foretold birth of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts signs accompanying the birth of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and links them to the future birth of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام. It presents Abū Ṭālib foretelling to Fāṭimah bint Asad that she would bear the Prophet’s وصيّ and وزير, highlighting the special rank of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام from before his birth.

en.hubeali: Some of our companions, from the one who mentioned it, from Ibn Mahboub, from Umar Bin Aban Al Kalby, from Al Mufazzal Bin Umar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘When (Syeda) Aamina<sup>as</sup> was blessed with Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, there were opened up (displayed) for, the white (houses) of Persian, and palaces of Syria (as having been conquered).

So (Syeda) Fatima<sup>asws</sup> Bint Asad<sup>as</sup>, mother<sup>asws</sup> of Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> came over to Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup>, smiling, giving glad tidings, and let him<sup>asws</sup> know what Aamina<sup>asws</sup> had said.

So Abu Talib<sup>asws</sup> said to her<sup>asws</sup>: ‘You<sup>asws</sup> are being astounded from this? You<sup>asws</sup> would be blessed with and bring up his<sup>saww</sup> successor<sup>asws</sup> and his<sup>saww</sup> Vizier’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah has narrated from al-Sayyariy from Muhammad ibn Jumhur from certain persons of our people from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Fatima, mother of Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) was the first woman who has said the following. migrated to the Messenger of Allah from Makka to Madina on foot. She was the most kind person to the Messenger of Allah She heard the Messenger of Allah say, “On the Day of Judgment people will be raised naked as they were born.” She said, “My goodness, what a shame!” The Messenger of Allah then said, “I will pray to Allah to resurrect you all dressed up.” She heard him speak of the constraint in the grave.” She then said, “ Alas! How pitiful is my weakness!” the Messenger of Allah said, “I will pray to Allah to make it easy for you.”
